title: Unified Evidence Runbook: Incident-Driven Access, Audit, and Retention
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary

This runbook defines a single, repeatable process for assembling, validating, and preserving compliance evidence when incidents involve access anomalies, data residency questions, or potential SDLC/process issues. It replaces ad-hoc evidence collection with a structured 'evidence manifest' approach that spans RBAC assertions, audit-log extractions, retention policy validation, and chain-of-custody handoff to Legal/Compliance.

Scope

- Applies to security incidents where any of the following are true: unauthorized access, privileged escalation, cross-region data movement, potential data retention violation, or CI/CD/supply-chain compromise.
- Covers evidence types: RBAC snapshots, authentication/session traces, audit logs (ingest, application, infra), storage access logs, retention policy configs, CI/CD pipeline run metadata, and related service artifacts.
- Intended audience: Incident Responders, Security Engineers, SREs, Privacy/Legal, and Evidence Custodians.

Ownership and Roles

- Incident Commander (IC): overall decision authority during an incident.
- Evidence Custodian (EC): responsible for collecting, verifying, and storing evidence artifacts. Typically a member of Security Ops.
- RBAC Owner: team-level owner responsible for role definitions and attestation.
- SRE/Platform Eng: performs log and snapshot exports for infra and network artifacts.
- Legal/Compliance Liaison: receives preserved evidence for regulatory review.

When to Use This Runbook

1. Authentication anomalies (suspicious logins, atypical session durations).
2. Unexpected data residency changes (object copies to new region, cross-account replication).
3. Privileged role misuse or suspected compromise.
4. Build pipeline or deployment artifacts that may have introduced malicious changes.

Pre-Incident Preparation (Checklist)

- Maintain a current Evidence Manifest template in the secure Evidence Store.
- Configure immutable audit log exports to the Evidence Archive (S3 with Object Lock or equivalent).
- Ensure RBAC role definitions and assignment snapshots are available via automated daily export (IAM snapshots).
- Retention policy matrix published and mapped to data classes (PII, PHI, telemetry, logs).
- Maintain contact roster for ECs, Legal, and SRE on-call.

Evidence Manifest (single-file canonical index)

The Evidence Manifest is a JSON or YAML file that references collected artifacts, includes collection metadata, and provides a tamper-evident hash list. Example manifest fields (presented here as a text table):

| field | description | example |
|---|---|---|
| incident_id | Unique incident identifier | INC-2026-0457 |
| manifest_version | Runbook schema version | v1.1 |
| collected_by | Name/email of Evidence Custodian | maya.chen@redwood.example.com |
| collection_time_utc | ISO8601 timestamp when manifest created | 2026-02-28T19:23:12Z |
| artifacts | List of artifact descriptors (type, storage_path, sha256) | see artifact examples below |

Artifact examples (plain text representation):
- type: iam_snapshot
  path: s3://evidence-archive/inc-2026-0457/iam-snapshot-20260228.json
  sha256: a3f5...
- type: auth_sessions_export
  path: gs://audit-exports/inc-2026-0457/sessions-20260228.ndjson
  sha256: b7c2...
- type: object_copy_log
  path: s3://object-logs/replication/rep-20260227.log
  sha256: 9d1a...

During Incident — Evidence Collection Procedure (numbered steps)

1) IC declares evidence collection required and assigns Evidence Custodian.
2) EC creates Evidence Manifest (populate incident_id, manifest_version, collected_by, collection_time_utc).
3) Snapshot RBAC: request IAM snapshot from RBAC Owner or run the certified snapshot script (see Appendix). Include role definitions, assignment mappings, and effective policies.
4) Export authentication/session traces for impacted accounts and time windows (retain full session start/end, originating IPs, MFA state, token IDs).
5) Pull audit logs for the affected services/time range: application logs, API gateway logs, database audit logs, and storage access logs. Prefer original, append-only exports where available.
6) If cross-region data movement suspected, export object replication logs and bucket-level event histories, and note the corresponding data classification.
7) Collect CI/CD artifacts if build or deploy is implicated: pipeline run logs, commit SHA, build artifact checksums, and signed release metadata.
8) For any encrypted keys or KMS operations, record KMS operation IDs (do not export customer plaintext keys).
9) For temporary or mutable systems, take forensic snapshots (disk images, container filesystem exports) following SRE/Forensics guidance.
10) Hash every artifact with SHA-256 and add the value to the manifest. Store hash and manifest in an append-only Evidence Archive.

Preservation and Chain-of-Custody

- Evidence Archive: S3 bucket (evidence-archive) configured with Object Lock (legal hold when escalated) and strict ACLs.
- Each evidence upload must include metadata tags: incident_id, artifact_type, collected_by, source_service, collection_timestamp.
- The EC must produce a signed Chain-of-Custody note (template available) and email it to Legal/Compliance; copy is stored in the Evidence Archive.

Audit-Logging Mapping Table

Provide quick mapping between observation types and required log sources:

| observation | primary logs | secondary/artifacts | minimum retention required |
| suspicious-auth | auth-service logs, idp access logs, mf*a logs | session traces, ip-reputation | 365 days for privileged accounts |
| data-replication | bucket replication logs, object-change events | object metadata, s3 access logs | 7 years for regulated datasets |
| admin-api-change | control-plane audit logs | terraform state, git commits | 3 years for compliance-sensitive ops |

RBAC Validation Procedures

- Run certified role-evaluator script (link and CLI in Appendix) to produce an effective permission matrix for implicated users.
- Confirm time-bounded temporary elevation records (e.g., SSO session policy, just-in-time grants) and attach approval artifacts.
- If a role appears misconfigured, mark the role as "suspect" in the manifest and include proposed rollback or remediation steps.

Data Residency and Retention Considerations

- When evidence includes cross-region movement: annotate the manifest with data classification and applicable residency rules (e.g., EU PII cannot be stored outside eu-1 for more than 24 hours).
- For expedited regulatory requests, the Legal Liaison may request a retention hold; EC must apply Object Lock / legal-hold tag immediately and confirm via manifest update.

Secure SDLC Tie-Ins

- If pipeline artifacts are collected, verify: commit author identity (2FA), CI job signer keys, and artifact signatures.
- Tag the manifest with a "supply_chain_risk" boolean if external dependencies or third-party packages are implicated.

Risk & Exceptions Guidance

- Low probability, high-impact deviation (e.g., emergency cross-region copy to prevent data loss) requires an exception ticket in the Risk Registry with EC/Legal approval. Attach the exception and post-facto evidence to the manifest.
- Routine temporary escalations should be pre-authorized via time-limited grants; log and persist those approvals as artifacts.

Post-Incident — Handoff and Retention

- EC updates manifest with final artifact locations and hashes and marks evidence status: collected | validated | released_to_legal.
- Legal/Compliance confirms receipt and sets long-term retention policy for the incident artifacts.
- If artifacts contain regulated data, annotate retention duration and access restrictions in the manifest and in the Evidence Archive tags.

Operational SLAs and SLOs for Evidence Collection

- Initial evidence manifest created within 2 hours of EC assignment.
- Primary audit-log exports available within 8 hours for on-cloud services; 24 hours for on-prem systems.
- Forensic snapshot availability within 24 hours if required.

Appendix: CLI Commands and Queries

- IAM snapshot (example):
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n    https://iam.redwood.internal/api/v1/snapshot > iam-snapshot-$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ).json

- S3 export (example):
  aws s3 cp s3://app-audit-logs/2026/02/28/ s3://evidence-archive/inc-2026-0457/audit-logs/ --recursive --storage-class DEEP_ARCHIVE

- SHA256 hash (example):
  sha256sum artifact-file.tar.gz | awk '{print $1}'

Appendix: Evidence Manifest template (minimal fields)

incident_id: "INC-YYYY-NNNN"
manifest_version: "v1.1"
collected_by: "name <email>"
collection_time_utc: "ISO8601"
artifacts: [ { type, path, sha256, collected_from, note } ]
chain_of_custody: { signed_by, datetime, notes }
